newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol says no plans to lift landing fees in 97.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol says no plans to lift landing fees in 97.

text.p: Schiphol Airport will not be increasing its landing fees this year, an airport spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

No changes are planned to any airport charges, with the exception of one guilder increase in the passenger transfer fee to 4.6 guilders from January 1. This rise is to reduce the difference between the fees of departing and transfer passengers, she told Reuters.

Air cargo volumes totalled 1.081 million tonnes in 1996, representing an increase of 10.6 percent. The airport expects this to increase by a further seven percent during this year, added the spokeswoman.

This year the Dutch airport plans to embark on a major terminal refurbishment at the cost of 500 million guilders over the next four years. As well as this, the airport also plans to invest in the new Schiphol South East Cargo World area.
